title: China: AI slowdown and anti-Chinese efforts are "fearmongering," "cold war playbook" - TCR 09/15/26
description:
China's foreign ministry called the AI slowdown essay "fearmongering" and a "Cold War playbook" as its spy chief outlined six AI risks, including threats to Communist Party rule, President Trump dismissed fears of AI taking over and destroying humanity as a "HOAX" while a bipartisan Congress readied a kill-switch bill, and ECB President Christine Lagarde told Europe to build its own AI or be cut off, citing Epoch AI's 2025 dataset, which placed about 75 percent of tracked AI-cluster performance in the US and less than 5 percent in the European Union.

https://sharedsapience.com/the-century-report-september-15-2026/

0:00 Open and framing
0:56 China rejects the AI slowdown call
4:06 Washington splits on AI guardrails
7:13 Europe's ECB says build your own AI
10:07 Definium's LSD therapy clears a third trial
13:15 A brain implant decodes speech and gesture
15:56 Close

This episode covers Beijing's rejection of the AI slowdown call, the split between the White House and Congress on AI guardrails, Christine Lagarde's warning on Europe's compute dependency, Definium's third Phase 3 win for single-dose LSD anxiety therapy, and a UCSF brain implant that decodes speech and gesture at once.

On Monday, September 14, Beijing answered the call to slow frontier AI, and it answered from both directions. China's foreign ministry dismissed the essay as fearmongering, a state newspaper called it a "Cold War playbook," and the minister of state security warned that AI threatens Communist Party rule, even as the essay itself asked Washington to tighten chip controls and keep democracies' lead "as large as possible." The containment case leaks: a Chinese reasoning model, built on a base model with a reported final training compute cost under $6 million, helped move US chip stocks. In Washington, President Trump called fears of AI taking over and destroying humanity a hoax while a Louisiana Republican readied a kill-switch bill and University of Maryland pollsters found roughly four in five voters of both parties want a federal AI monitor. From Vienna, Christine Lagarde told Europe to build its own models or accept being cut off. And the acceleration kept producing: Definium's single-dose LSD therapy cleared a third Phase 3 toward the first psychedelic approved for anxiety, a UCSF implant decoded speech and gesture together for a paralyzed user, and NVIDIA's Rubin platform posted up to seven times the work per megawatt with its benchmark open-sourced.
